Each Act that is specified in a Schedule to this Act is amended or repealed as set out in the applicable items in the Schedule concerned, and any other item in a Schedule to this Act has effect according to its terms.

Repeal the section, substitute:
This Part is about the accountable authorities and officials of Commonwealth entities.
Accountable authorities
There are general duties that apply to all accountable authorities. Those duties are set out in sections 15 to 19.
Accountable authorities may give instructions to officials under section 20A. Those instructions are part of the finance law.

In relation to whether accountable authorities must apply government policy, different requirements apply depending on whether the entity is a non-corporate Commonwealth entity (see section 21) or a corporate Commonwealth entity (see section 22).
The accountable authorities of non-corporate Commonwealth entities have power to enter into arrangements, and approve commitments of relevant money, on behalf of the Commonwealth (see section 23).
Officials
There are general duties that apply to all officials. Those duties are set out in sections 25 to 29.

If an official who is the accountable authority, or a member of the accountable authority, of a corporate Commonwealth entity contravenes those duties, the official’s appointment may be terminated (see section 30).

content.p: Insert:
Subdivision BA—Accountable authority instructions
The accountable authority of a Commonwealth entity may, by written instrument, give instructions to an official of the entity about any matter relating to the finance law.
The accountable authority of a Commonwealth entity may, by written instrument, give instructions to an official of another Commonwealth entity in relation to:
the official approving the commitment of relevant money for which the accountable authority is responsible; and
the official banking, or otherwise dealing with, relevant money for which the accountable authority is responsible; and
the official debiting or crediting an appropriation for which the accountable authority is responsible; and
any matter prescribed by the rules that relates to the official dealing with public resources for which the accountable authority is responsible.
An instruction under subsection (1) or (2) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Banking or dealing with relevant money

content.p: Ministers

A Minister who receives relevant money (other than relevant money that is to be held for the purposes of making payments in relation to the Minister’s official duties) must give the money to an official of a non-corporate Commonwealth entity as soon as is practicable.
Officials receiving bankable money
(2) An official of a Commonwealth entity who receives relevant money that can be deposited in a bank (bankable money) must:
deposit the bankable money in a bank:
within the period prescribed by the rules or, if the rules do not prescribe a period, as soon as is practicable; and
in accordance with any requirements prescribed by the rules; or
otherwise deal with the bankable money in accordance with any requirements prescribed by the rules.
Officials receiving unbankable money
The rules may prescribe matters relating to relevant money that:
is received by an official of a Commonwealth entity; and
is not bankable money.
Application of section
To avoid doubt, this section applies to money that becomes relevant money on receipt by a Minister or an official of a Commonwealth entity.

section.heading: Waiver of amounts or modification of payment terms

content.p: The Finance Minister may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, authorise:
the waiver of an amount owing to the Commonwealth; or
the modification of the terms and conditions on which an amount owing to the Commonwealth is to be paid to the Commonwealth.
An authorisation of a waiver or modification must be in accordance with any requirements prescribed by the rules.
An authorisation of a waiver may be made either unconditionally or on the condition that a person agrees to pay an amount to the Commonwealth in specified circumstances.
To avoid doubt, an amount may be owing to the Commonwealth even if it is not yet due for payment.
An authorisation of a waiver or modification is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Instruments relating to intelligence or security agencies or listed law enforcement agencies

content.p: (1) This section applies in relation to an activity (the designated activity) determined under subsection (2) of the following entities:
an intelligence or security agency that is a Commonwealth entity;
a listed law enforcement agency that is a Commonwealth entity;
a Commonwealth entity of which a part is an intelligence or security agency.
Determination of designated activities

The responsible Minister for a Commonwealth entity referred to in subsection (1) may, by written instrument, determine that an activity of the entity is a designated activity if the Minister is satisfied that the activity is engaged in for the purposes of:
for paragraph (1)(a) or (b)—the entity; or
for paragraph (1)(c)—the part of the entity.
Determination modifying this Act and other instruments
The Finance Minister may determine, by written instrument, modifications of the following in relation to a designated activity of a Commonwealth entity:
Part 2-3 (which deals with planning, performance and accountability);
Part 2-4 (which deals with the management of public resources);
Part 2-7 (which deals with companies, subsidiaries and new corporate Commonwealth entities);
Chapter 3 (which deals with Commonwealth companies);
any other provision of this Act prescribed by the rules;
the rules;
an instrument made under section 105B or 105C (which deal with procurement and grants).
Note: Modifications is defined in section 2B of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.
A determination under subsection (3) that relates to a Commonwealth entity may also include:
a delegation of a power, function or duty under section 107 to an official of the entity; and
any direction to the official under that section.
Review of determinations
A determination under subsection (2) or (3) must be reviewed:
at least once every 3 years; or
if the activities of the entity change significantly.
Determinations not legislative instruments
A determination under subsection (2) or (3) is not a legislative instrument.
